extraFacts.fact: SAE J518 and ISO 6162 cover four-bolt split-flange connections in two pressure series: Code 61 (the 3000 psi series, ISO 6162-1) and Code 62 (the 6000 psi series, ISO 6162-2). A Code 61 flange head is not interchangeable with a Code 62 clamp, because the bolt spacing differs for the same nominal size.

316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A240 / A276 chemical composition limits for UNS S31603

faqs.q: What is the SAE counter-flange used for?
faqs.a: The SAE counter-flange is a 316L stainless-steel SAE J518 four-bolt flange, the mating piece for an SAE flange head, in sizes from 1/2" to 2" and listed as Code 62. It is the flange half that bolts to the flange head on a hose end or port, so a hose assembly can be fitted to a pump, valve or manifold with split-flange bolting.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the SAE counter-flange come in?
faqs.a: The SAE counter-flange is listed from 1/2" to 2". The listing has no part-number table, so send the SAE flange size and code (61 or 62) on the equipment side, and we confirm the right counter-flange.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right SAE counter-flange for a port?
faqs.a: Match the flange size and the code to the equipment port: the listing says Code 62, and a Code 61 head will not fit a Code 62 counter-flange. Send us the port's size and code, or the pump or valve model, and we confirm it.

faqs.q: What pressure is the SAE counter-flange rated for?
faqs.a: The listing gives L-series 210 bar (3000 psi) and S-series 415 bar (6000 psi) for the SAE counter-flange. The rating of a flange joint is set by the SAE J518 code and the host port, so confirm the port's code and pressure, and keep the assembly within the hose rating as well.

faqs.q: What is the SAE counter-flange made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The SAE counter-flange is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. It suits marine, chemical, food-grade and washdown service where zinc-plated carbon steel corrodes. The listing gives -40°C to +200°C, limited by the hose and any O-ring.

faqs.q: Which standards does the SAE counter-flange follow?
faqs.a: The SAE counter-flange is listed to SAE J518 and ISO 6162. They cover four-bolt split-flange connections in Code 61 (3000 psi) and Code 62 (6000 psi), with the bolt pattern fixed by the code and size.

faqs.q: What does the SAE counter-flange connect to?
faqs.a: It mates with an SAE flange head, such as the [SAE flange](/p/sae-flange), using the O-ring from the [seals for 3000-6000 psi flanges](/p/seals-for-3000-6000-psi-flange). For fully stainless assemblies pair it with 316L bolts and an SS316L hose end; see our [stainless crimp hose fittings](/c/stainless-crimp-hose-fittings).

faqs.q: How is an SAE counter-flange bolted up?
faqs.a: Fit the O-ring in the groove of the flange head, offer the counter-flange square and tighten the four bolts evenly in a cross pattern. Use stainless bolts on a stainless joint, and replace the O-ring whenever the joint is opened.

faqs.q: Where is a stainless SAE counter-flange used?
faqs.a: It is used on stainless hydraulic and process lines with SAE flange ports in marine, chemical and washdown plant, where plated steel flanges would corrode. The [galvanic corrosion in fittings](/blog/galvanic-corrosion-in-fittings) guide covers mixing metals.

faqs.q: SAE counter-flange or SAE split flange: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The SAE counter-flange is the mating flange half, while the [SAE split flange](/p/sae-split-flange) is the clamp-style flange that holds a flange head to the port. Both are for SAE J518 joints, so check which half the joint needs.

faqs.a: The listing gives it as Code 62, the 6000 psi series, but the pressure line quotes both L-series and S-series ratings. Measure the bolt spacing against the SAE J518 table or read the code from the port, and confirm with us; [3000 psi SAE straight flange, Code 61](/p/3000-psi-sae-straight-flange-code-61) is the Code 61 alternative.

faqs.q: What pressure is the SAE flange rated for?

faqs.q: Which standards does the SAE flange follow?

faqs.q: How do I fit an SAE flange and keep the O-ring from leaking?
faqs.a: Check the O-ring is seated in its groove and undamaged, seat the flange head square on the port and tighten the four bolts evenly in a cross pattern. Do not reuse a flattened O-ring, and replace it whenever the joint is opened.

faqs.q: How should SAE split flange bolts be tightened?

faqs.q: How do I replace a flange O-ring without damaging it?
faqs.a: Remove the old O-ring, clean the groove and sealing faces, fit the new O-ring without twisting or stretching it, and tighten the four flange bolts evenly in a cross pattern. Replace the seal every time the joint is opened.
